heading: The families Joseph and Emma called home
introduction: Before they made a home together, Joseph and Emma belonged to two large families. Their parents, brothers and sisters shaped the places and relationships from which their married life began. Their own children brought both joy and deep sorrow.

Follow the two families separately, then the children Joseph and Emma raised and remembered. Each name belongs to a different lifetime; these records let us hold those lives together without losing their dates.

families.heading: Joseph’s parents, brothers and sisters
paragraphs: Joseph Smith Sr. (12 July 1771–14 September 1840) and Lucy Mack Smith (8 July 1775–14 May 1856) married on 24 January 1796. Their eleven children included Joseph, his older brother Hyrum, and two sons who died in infancy.

The names also reveal how closely loss touched this family. Alvin died in 1823. Don Carlos died in 1841. Joseph and Hyrum died on the same day in June 1844, and Samuel died the following month. Their mother, Lucy Mack Smith, lived until 1856.

families.heading: Emma’s parents, brothers and sisters
paragraphs: Isaac Hale (21 March 1763–11 January 1839) and Elizabeth Lewis Hale (19 November 1767–16 February 1842) married on 20 September 1790. Emma was the seventh of their nine children.

Their home stood in Pennsylvania’s Susquehanna Valley. Emma’s childhood began in the family’s log home; the later frame house was built around 1809. When Joseph and Emma moved to Harmony in 1827, they returned to the region and relationships she had known growing up.

families.heading: Joseph and Emma’s children
paragraphs: Joseph and Emma’s family included nine children born to Emma and the two Murdock twins they adopted. In 1831, Emma’s newborn twins died. John Murdock’s wife, Julia Clapp, died after giving birth to twins that same day; Joseph and Emma welcomed those children, Julia and Joseph, into their home.

Several of their children died very young. Julia, Joseph III, Frederick, Alexander and David Hyrum lived into adulthood. David was born in November 1844, after his father’s death. Their family story therefore continues beyond the years Joseph and Emma shared.
members: Julia M. Smith, adopted Murdock twin
families.note: The familiar names Alvin, Louisa and Thadeus were added to the family Bible later by another hand. Joseph and Emma did not record names for the 1831 twins, and Emma later described them as unnamed. Joseph’s son Don Carlos is distinct from his younger brother of the same name.
